root_cause_criterion.criterion: Before `krb5_pac_parse()` may continue into PAC buffer parsing, the claimed descriptor count `cbuffers` must fit the available header bytes without relying on the overflow-prone `cbuffers * PAC_INFO_BUFFER_LENGTH` arithmetic.
root_cause_criterion.description: The vulnerable original evaluates this predicate as false (`268435456 <= 0`) yet still reaches `buffer->cbBufferSize = load_32_le(p)`. The fixed original is guarded at the new `cbuffers` check, and the adjacent `one_complete_descriptor` witness executes the protected sink with the predicate true (`1 <= 1`).

nodes.state: At `buffer->cbBufferSize = load_32_le(p)`, the source-level 4-byte read width exceeds the remaining logical input bytes starting at `p`, so the sink reads past the 15-byte PAC blob.

edges.relation: The same attacker-controlled local `cbuffers` value recorded at the root guard site is installed into the heap PAC header field that the loop later reads.
The installed heap field remains the loop bound when the first `PAC_INFO_BUFFER` body begins, so descriptor parsing proceeds under the same claimed count.
After the first descriptor field read succeeds, the advanced parser cursor `p` is reused unchanged as the argument to the next 4-byte `cbBufferSize` read.
